title: The 'Promising Failure' of the First Car to Carry Ferrari's Name
conflicts: Departure from Alfa Romeo: 6 September 1939 (Ludvigsen/Revs and Ferrari's own timeline) against 1938 (Goodwood; Jenkinson dates the falling-out to 1938); the story uses September 1939. Wartime bombing: Ferrari's timeline says 4 November 1944 and the following February, Motor Sport (2014) twice in the closing weeks of 1944; the story follows Ferrari. Colombo commission: mid-1945 (Ferrari magazine 2019) against late 1945 (Ferrari timeline 2016); the story says 1945. Win totals for 1947 differ between two ferrari.com pages; the story names only the wins Motor Sport lists. Machine tools are 'milling' in Motor Sport and 'grinding' in Ferrari's timeline; the story says machine tools.
notes: ferrari.com and corporate.ferrari.com block automated requests, so Ferrari's own pages are cited through Internet Archive copies, which load. The Motor Web Museum page wrongly dates the Piacenza debut to March and is not cited. Cortese's 'You'd have to be crazy' warning is reported by Richard Williams in Motor Sport (2014) and is quoted as Cortese's words, not Ferrari's. The 1943 date for the Maranello move comes from Ferrari's 2016 timeline.
